# Isolated Cargo Target Directory per Worktree

Playbook: PB-3 Scoped Fix. No ADR. The change stays inside the existing
`scripts/worktree.ts` and `cargo-worktree-hygiene` boundaries.

## 1. Problem Statement

Commit `6fd20d5` added a worktree pool config file. `worktree.ts` writes it to
`<pool>/.cargo/config.toml` with this content:

```toml
# Generated by worktree.ts for automatic shared target cache & concurrency hygiene
[build]
target-dir = "<repoRoot>/target"
jobs = N
```

Cargo finds this file from every worktree in the pool. As a result, all
worktrees and the main checkout use one shared target directory. The goal was
to reduce disk use and reuse compiled dependencies.

This sharing is not safe for workspace crates:

1. Cargo gives a workspace crate the same artifact and fingerprint names in
   every checkout. The names use paths relative to the workspace root, not
   absolute paths.
2. Cargo checks freshness of a local crate by file modification time. It
   compares the source files with the last build output.
3. Worktree A builds at time T. Worktree B has sources with an older
   modification time. Cargo marks B as fresh and B runs the artifacts of A.

Registry dependencies are identified by version and checksum. They are safe
to share. Only path and workspace crates have this problem.

Observed effect in a consumer Rust repository (2026-10-12): builders got false
test failures and wrong test counts. They had to set a separate
`CARGO_TARGET_DIR` for each worktree.

The shared directory also does not help parallel builds. Cargo locks
`target/<profile>/` for the full build. Two builders that use the same
directory and profile wait for each other.

These claims were checked against Cargo 1.97.1. Check them again if Cargo
makes checksum-based freshness (`-Zchecksum-freshness`) stable.

## 2. Decision

- Each worktree uses its own `target/` directory. This is the Cargo default.
- `worktree.ts` does not write `target-dir` to the pool config.
- The pool config keeps `jobs`, which still controls CPU use.
- `worktree env` does not export a target directory path. An exported path
  stays set after `cd` and makes the next checkout share it.
- Disk use stays controlled by the existing pre-flight disk guard, the
  `hygiene` report, and `target/` removal in `worktree remove`.
- Optional dependency caching uses a content-hashed tool such as `sccache`.
  The tool is documentation only. `worktree.ts` does not configure it.

**Intentional behavior changes:**

- Worktrees no longer share a target directory. The first build in each
  worktree compiles all dependencies. Do not add a flag that restores the
  shared target directory.
- `worktree env` prints `unset CARGO_TARGET_DIR` instead of an
  `export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=...` line. Scripts that `eval` the output still
  work.

## 3. Rules

These rules apply. The tasks and tests refer to them by ID.

- **R1 — New pool config.** When `ensureCargoPoolConfig` creates the config
  file, the file contains this header, `[build]`, and `jobs = N`. It does not
  contain `target-dir` or `build-dir`.
  ```text
  # Generated by worktree.ts for Cargo concurrency hygiene. Each worktree keeps its own target/ directory.
  ```
- **R2 — Legacy migration.** A legacy file is a file whose first line, after
  removal of a trailing `\r`, is exactly
  `# Generated by worktree.ts for automatic shared target cache & concurrency hygiene`.
  For a legacy file, `ensureCargoPoolConfig`:
  1. replaces the first line with the R1 header;
  2. removes each line that matches `^\s*(build\.)?target-dir\s*=`;
  3. keeps all other lines unchanged and in the same order, including
     `jobs` and any keys that a user added;
  4. writes one line to stderr:
     `worktree: removed shared target-dir from <path>; each worktree now uses its own target/`.
  Running the migration a second time does not change the file. The new
  header is not the legacy header.
- **R3 — User files are preserved.** `ensureCargoPoolConfig` does not modify a
  file that does not start with the legacy header. This applies also when the
  file sets `target-dir`.
- **R4 — Hygiene reports target isolation.** `worktree hygiene` prints one
  `Cargo Target Isolation:` line. The checks are:
  - the pool config has a non-comment line that matches
    `^\s*(build\.)?(target-dir|build-dir)\s*=`;
  - one of the environment variables `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`,
    `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET_DIR`, or `CARGO_BUILD_BUILD_DIR` is set and not empty.
  If no check matches, the state is
  `isolated (checked: pool config, environment)`. Otherwise print
  `shared` and one indented line for each match: the file path or the
  variable name and value. Then print one warning line:
  `Shared Cargo build output lets one checkout reuse stale artifacts of another.`
  The command does not read `$CARGO_HOME/config.toml` or ancestor
  `.cargo/config.toml` files. The `checked:` text states this limit.
- **R5 — Hygiene reports target sizes.** `worktree hygiene` prints the size of
  `<checkout>/target` for every checkout in `git worktree list`, including the
  main checkout. Label the main checkout `(main)`. Skip a checkout that has no
  `target/`. Print the total. If `du` fails for a checkout, print `unknown`
  for it and continue. The command still exits with code 0.
- **R6 — `env` does not export a target path.** `worktree env [n]` prints
  `export CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=<n>` as before. Then it prints
  `unset CARGO_TARGET_DIR CARGO_BUILD_TARGET_DIR`. It prints no path.
- **R7 — Documentation matches behavior.** No active document tells users to
  share one target directory across worktrees. No active document says that a
  separate `target/` per worktree is a failure mode.

## 4. Tasks

### Task 1: Pool config and migration (R1, R2, R3)

Files: `scripts/worktree.ts`.

- Change the content that `ensureCargoPoolConfig` writes for a new file to the
  R1 content.
- Add the R2 legacy detection and line-level migration. Keep a `jobs` value
  exactly as written. Do not parse it.
- Keep the function return contract: `true` when the function wrote the file,
  `false` otherwise.
- Keep the call sites in `getWorktreesDir` unchanged.

### Task 2: Hygiene report (R4, R5)

Files: `scripts/worktree.ts`.

- Replace the `Shared Cargo Target:` line with the R4 output.
- Detect keys with line matches. Ignore lines whose first non-space character
  is `#`. Do not add a TOML parser dependency.
- Get sizes with `du -sk <path>` for each checkout from `listWorktrees`. Print
  sizes in GB with one decimal place.
- Put the size lookup in a small exported function, so the `unknown` branch
  stays readable. A test for the `unknown` branch is not required.

### Task 4: Tests (R1–R6)

Files: `tests/worktree.test.ts`.

Test isolation requirements. These apply to every new test and to the
existing test `executes hygiene and env commands successfully`:

- A test that calls `main()` must `process.chdir()` into the temporary
  repository or worktree first. It restores the previous directory in
  `finally`. A test must not run `hygiene` against the sirius-skills checkout.
- A test that checks R4 saves `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET_DIR`,
  and `CARGO_BUILD_BUILD_DIR`. It deletes them at the start and restores them
  in `finally`.
- Capture `console.log` and `console.error` with a spy. Restore them in
  `finally`.
- Do not use `test.concurrent`. The working directory and the environment are
  process-global.
- Compare paths after `realpathSync`, because a temporary directory can be a
  symbolic link (for example on macOS).
- Use real files and real git worktrees, like the existing tests. Do not mock
  `existsSync`, `writeFileSync`, or `git`.

Replace the test `automatically provisions shared cargo config when Cargo.toml exists`.
Add tests with these names:

- `writes pool cargo config with jobs and without target-dir` (R1)
- `migrates legacy pool config and keeps jobs and user keys` (R2). Include a
  user key such as `[env]` and a CRLF first line. Assert the stderr notice.
- `legacy migration is idempotent` (R2)
- `does not modify user-authored pool config that sets target-dir` (R3)
- `hygiene reports shared target from user-authored pool config` (R4). Use a
  non-legacy file, because `hygiene` migrates a legacy file first.
- `hygiene reports dotted build.target-dir in pool config` (R4)
- `hygiene reports CARGO_TARGET_DIR override` (R4)
- `hygiene reports isolated when no override exists` (R4)
- `hygiene reports target size for main checkout and worktree` (R5). Create
  small `target/` files in both.
- `env prints jobs and unsets target overrides without a path` (R6)

## 5. Out of Scope

- Configuring `sccache` or any other cache in `worktree.ts`.
- Changing the disk guard thresholds (5 GB and 15 GB).
- Adding a pool config to pools set by environment variable or git config.
  The current code does not write a config there. Keep that behavior.
- Reading `$CARGO_HOME/config.toml` or ancestor Cargo config files in
  `hygiene`. R4 states the checked scope.
- Pool detection from inside a worktree. `detectWorktreePool` can select the
  parent directory of the main checkout when only one other worktree exists.
  This is an existing defect. Run `hygiene` from the main checkout. Track the
  defect separately.
- Cleaning target directories in consumer repositories. See section 7.

## 6. Verification

The builder runs these commands in the worktree and reports the output:

```bash
bun test tests/worktree.test.ts
bun test tests
rg -niE "shar(ed|ing)[^\n]{0,20}target|target[^\n]{0,20}shar|target (storage|cache)" skills catalog scripts README.md PROMPT_GUIDE.md
git diff --stat
```

Acceptance:

- All tests pass. Each rule R1–R6 has at least one test from Task 4.
- No test changes files or directories in the sirius-skills checkout outside
  temporary directories.
- Each `rg` match is a warning against shared targets or the R4 output text.
  No match recommends sharing a target directory.
- `git diff --stat` shows changes only in the files named in Tasks 1–5.

## 7. Operator Follow-up After Merge (Not a Builder Task)

These steps apply to each consumer repository that used the old pool config.

1. Update the `external/sirius-skills` submodule in `thinker`.
2. Run `bun scripts/worktree.ts hygiene` from the main checkout of the
   consumer repository. This migrates the generated pool config (R2) and
   reports the target state.
3. The main checkout `target/` can contain artifacts from other branches. Run
   `cargo clean` once in the main checkout.
4. Remove merged worktrees with `bun scripts/worktree.ts remove <branch> -d` to
   recover disk space.
